title: Runtime: emit build + kernel selection/version tags in telemetry
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Context: perf-canary + SRE triage needs to quickly answer “what changed?” when p95 latency or tokens/sec regresses. Today we can see model/version + hardware, but we can’t reliably correlate to runtime build or kernel selection changes (especially when selection is dynamic). This PR adds low-cardinality tags to runtime telemetry (metrics + traces + request debug logs) to identify the runtime build and the kernel selection outcome for a request. These tags are explicitly designed for per-model aggregation and alert attribution and should be stable across rollouts. What’s included: (1) Runtime build tags: runtime.build_id (semver-ish build label from build pipeline), runtime.git_sha (short SHA), runtime.build_flavor (release|debug), runtime.feature_set (compile-time feature bitset exported as a short string; see below). (2) Kernel selection identifiers: kernel.bundle_version (version string for the kernel pack baked into the runtime image), kernel.selector_version (version for selection logic), kernel.policy (e.g. auto|pinned|compat), kernel.id (stable identifier for the chosen kernel impl), kernel.variant (e.g. fp16|bf16|int8 where applicable). (3) Guardrails to keep cardinality bounded: kernel.id is a curated stable name (NOT a per-build hash), kernel.variant is a small enum, runtime.feature_set is a fixed-format string with a bounded keyspace. We intentionally do NOT tag with full PTX/cubin hashes or per-host identifiers. (4) Backward compatibility: all tags are optional; exporters will omit on older runtimes. Dashboards/queries can use label_replace/defaults safely. (5) Tests: unit tests for tag formatting + allowed-value validation, and a golden telemetry test that asserts emitted label set for a representative request. Notes/decisions: - runtime.build_id source of truth is the build pipeline env var RUNTIME_BUILD_ID (already present in release builds but not previously emitted). We fall back to “unknown” in dev builds to avoid breaking local runs. - kernel.bundle_version is sourced from kernels/manifest.json embedded at build time; selector_version is incremented with changes to heuristics (documented in code). - For tracing, we add these as span attributes on the “runtime.decode” and “runtime.prefill” spans (not per-token spans) to avoid overhead. - For metrics, tags are applied only to the canary/perf aggregation metrics and a small set of existing runtime histograms that are already sampled/aggregated; we did not add tags to high-volume per-request counters. Rollout: safe to ship behind TELEMETRY_EMIT_RUNTIME_KERNEL_TAGS=true (default on in prod builds after this merges). We can flip it off quickly if there’s any telemetry cost surprise. Follow-ups: update perf-canary dashboard links and alert payload formatter to include these fields (separate PR in incident-bot/observability-pack).
commits: runtime/telemetry: plumb build metadata into TelemetryContext
runtime/kernels: embed manifest + export bundle version
runtime/kernels: add stable kernel.id + variant mapping
runtime/tracing: attach build/kernel attrs to prefill/decode spans
runtime/metrics: gate + add bounded labels to perf histograms
tests: golden telemetry snapshot + label allowlist tests
docs: inline comment + runbook note for interpreting tags
illustrative_snippet: New metric label set (bounded): model, model_version, region, hardware_sku, runtime_build_id, kernel_bundle_version, kernel_id, kernel_variant. Example trace attrs: runtime.build_id=2026.01.14.3, runtime.git_sha=3f2a91c, kernel.bundle_version=kpack-17, kernel.selector_version=6, kernel.policy=auto, kernel.id=flashattn_v3_sm90, kernel.variant=bf16.
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Kernel.id needs to be stable across rebuilds; do not use hash of binary. Also, avoid tagging by “kernel_path” because that will explode. Omar El-Sayed: Agree. Updated to use a curated enum in kernel_ids.h and mapping in selector; removed path-based tag. Added allowlist test to prevent regressions. Sofia Ivanova: Please confirm these labels aren’t added to high-volume queueing metrics; we already have tight budgets there. Omar El-Sayed: Confirmed. Labels are only on perf histograms (sampled) and canary-focused series; queueing counters remain unchanged. Added comment in runtime_metrics.cc. Logan Wright: Two concerns: (1) runtime.feature_set string risks high cardinality if it changes frequently, (2) kernel.selector_version should be documented; otherwise people will assume bundle_version implies selection logic. Omar El-Sayed: Addressed by making feature_set a fixed-format bitset with bounded combinations (currently 7 flags), and by adding selector_version + inline docs. Also updated golden telemetry snapshot. Nadia Rahman: Baseline store will join on these values; can we ensure “unknown” doesn’t end up in prod? Omar El-Sayed: In release builds RUNTIME_BUILD_ID is always set (added assert + warning if missing). “unknown” only for dev/local builds. Added a unit test that release builds set build_id via env var injection in CI. Approvals: Hiro approved after enum change. Logan approved after sampling/label scope clarification. Sofia approved with note to watch telemetry cost. Nadia approved for baseline pipeline compatibility.
release_notes: Runtime telemetry now includes runtime build identifiers and kernel selection identifiers (bounded labels) to improve attribution of performance regressions to releases/kernels (perf-canary + SRE triage).
